_comment: Indicator reference VALUES captured from a trusted GeoDMS build. The report (batch/generic/regression.py) judges each version's measurement against these at 0% tolerance. Regenerate deliberately via batch/capture_references.py after a trusted-build run; a normal test run never writes this file. Epoch-map thresholds may carry a flavor prefix ('l:0.0.0') = a PLATFORM baseline: it applies only to cells of that flavor and then takes precedence over the unprefixed epochs (t710 on Linux). Timing and memory (the mem/dur badges) are judged against the _captured_from run, never against a value epoch; _perf_epochs moves that one baseline for both: '*' = every test (an accepted engine step; the epoch's own cell shows the step it accepts), '<test>' = that test only (the test itself does different work from there on, so its cell is not compared back).

18.1.2.note: GeoDMS 18 changed its memory management; the step in peak committed memory from the 17.4.6 run to the 18.1.2 run (short tests re-measured 2026-10-01: t300 +33%, t405.1 +33%, t710 and t910 +9%, the rest within run-to-run noise) was accepted per Maarten, 2026-10-01: more memory is fine when it buys speed, a slowdown never is. Duration shares the baseline, so what this cell shows in red for t010 (+21%) and t641.1 (+18%) is a pure slowdown that came along; both run on the page file (170-310 GB committed on a 64 GB host) and are noisy. NB a single run is a noisy baseline: t300 on 18.1.2 took 2.1 min in August and 1.2 min today.

20.3.0.note: t020 runs its CBS/BAG part only from 20.3 on (_POLY_REAL_MIN_VERSION in full.py; below that just the synthetic part), so duration and memory restart here instead of comparing different work

20.20.0.note: from 20.20 t020 also runs the dms family (supported := GeoDmsVersion() >= 20.20 in Polygons/cfg/compare.dms), a fifth reader next to geos/bg/bp/cgal

20.3.0.note: t020 vergelijkt de families pas volledig vanaf 20.3: daaronder past area() de gridset-projectie niet toe (bp x1e4/1e6) en draait alleen het synthetische deel.

20.22.1.note: Accepted 20.22.1 baseline (ObjectVision/GeoDMS#1290): connect gives a point its nearest arc and, of equally near arcs, the one with the lowest index. It took the first arc the spatial index visited, an order that changed with the split threshold of 16 (#1289), and its float32 search box could leave out an arc a few mm nearer. PC6 points against the 20.22.1 build before #1289 (fd30ef780): 707 on another arc at the same distance, all now the lower index (-2 points), 16 on an arc 0.1 to 28 mm nearer, none farther (+21 points). The same value at split thresholds 4 and 16 (OVSRV05, 2026-10-04).

Accepted 20.22.1 baseline (ObjectVision/GeoDMS#1290): the OD cells follow from the PC6 network that connect builds, which since #1290 gives a point its nearest arc and, of equally near arcs, the one with the lowest index (see t100). The same value at split thresholds 4 and 16 (OVSRV05, 2026-10-04).

Accepted 20.22.1 baseline by decision, not by rule: these values record which polygon point_in_polygon finds first among overlapping ones, an order that follows from the spatial index (ObjectVision/GeoDMS#1290: which of several polygons it gives is unspecified). 20.22.1 splits a node from 16 objects instead of 4 (#1289); built with 4, the same commit 15651313f gives the 18.1.2 values exactly, at 16 these (OVSRV05, 2026-10-04). A change to the index may move them again; a different value from 20.22.1 on is first a question of order, not of the model.

It is NOT the DistFromOpt null-suitability fix of 20.19.1, which only corrects a status message and cannot change an allocation; the base-year Woningen/Banen come from t641_1 base data rather than discrete_alloc, so more than one subsystem moved. Cause not attributed.
